newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom disappointed by ratings downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Telecom disappointed by ratings downgrade.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Friday that it was disappointed by Standard & Poor's downgrade of its long-term rating to AA from AA+.

"While Telecom is disappointed by the rating downgrade announced by Standard & Poor's today, we are also pleased to see the agency acknowledged that Telecom's strong and diverse revenue base, which provides a fundamental strength to the ratings, is not expected to change in the medium-term," chief financial officer Jeff White said.
S&P said the downgrade was in light of Telecom's NZ$1 billion share buyback plan due for implementation this month.

White said S&P referred to Telecom's pre-tax interest cover ratio immediately following the share repurchase. He noted that ratio would still be higher than it was when Telecom's domestic debt was rated AA+ by S&P in 1991 and 1994.

"The revised credit rating of AA which Standard & Poor's has assigned, taking full account of the share repurchase and financing, indicates that Telecom's balance sheet is well able to accommodate the programme," White said.
